strategies.name: Opening-range breakout with a volume filter, long only (Zarattini, Barbon & Aziz 2024)
strategies.explain: PRE-REGISTERED, one version, resolved from the ORIGINAL paper before any run (Zarattini, Barbon & Aziz 2024, "A Profitable Day Trading Strategy for the U.S. Equity Market": 5-minute opening range on "stocks in play" = unusually high first-5-minute volume vs the prior 14 days, 7,000+ stocks, 2016-2023, Sharpe about 2.4; the GitHub 20-minute / 1.2x-volume version is a variant, not the paper). Record the exact spec and source for every element (range length, volume baseline, entry fill, target, stop, trail, 15:50 flat, long only, eligible universe, costs incl. spread and slippage) BEFORE looking at results; ambiguity is resolved from the source, never by what backtests best. Universe: the 100 most traded US stocks by dollar volume per test day (point-in-time), 2 years of Massive minute bars (budget the calls). Report: trades, distinct days, distinct stocks, median, worst trade, worst day, busiest-day exposure, same-catalyst concentration, result at 0.8% / 1.2% cost and with 0.1% extra slippage, latency table (fill delayed 0 / 1 / 5 / 15 / 30 minutes), without 2 best trades, vs the same stock open-to-close on its other days and the average stock the same day, both halves, league bar. A marginal pass still goes to PAPER first (execution decides intraday rules).
strategies.note: From the 21 Oct reviews (daily-trading redesign, ORB evidence).
strategies.study: orb-study.mjs -> data/orb-study.json (run once, first complete run frozen)
strategies.spec: RESOLVED 21 Oct 2026 from the original paper (SSRN 4729284, PDF read): opening range 9:30-9:35 (5 one-minute bars); direction = sign of the 5-minute candle, doji = no order; entry = stop order at the range high, filled at max(range high, bar open) on the first bar from 9:35 whose high exceeds it, no entry after 15:30; stop = entry minus 10% of the 14-day ATR; NO profit target, NO trailing stop (the paper has none); exit at the close; filters open > 5 USD, 14-day average volume 1M+ shares, ATR14 > 0.50 USD; relative volume = first-5-minute volume / its 14-session average, >= 1 (100%), top 20 by relative volume; paper sizing 1% risk and 4x leverage NOT reproduced (1,000 USD a trade); our costs 0.8% / 1.2% / 0.9% extra slippage; LONG ONLY; universe first the 100 most traded by previous-day dollar volume (minute-bar budget).

provisional.why: the stop at 10% of ATR14 sits 0.2-0.3% under the entry on liquid stocks, so 90% of trades are stopped within minutes for a tiny gross loss; at our 0.8% round-trip cost (the paper assumes 0.0035 USD a share and no slippage) the rule cannot pay by construction. Frozen verdict after the cache completes next Sunday.

strategies.name: Event, then opening-range retest (5-minute bars, delayed data)
strategies.explain: Only on days with a timestamped primary event (8-K acceptance time or issuer release). Opening range = first three completed 5-minute bars after the event is observable (bar close + 15-minute delay). Retest: touches no more than 0.2% above the range high, closes above it, never trades at or below the range low; confirmation bar closes above the retest high and session VWAP. Tested on the minute-bar cache against the same stock on non-event days and the average stock the same minutes. strategies.name: The 10x study (first stage of the 100x aim): early evidence, not past winners
strategies.explain: Pre-specify first: 10x = sustained (close held 10x for 20+ sessions), adjusted prices, min 2 USD and 200k shares/day at the start, whole market incl. dead stocks. For every 10x winner in 5 years record what was visible 12, 6 and 3 months BEFORE the move, using only data dated then, in six families: business acceleration (revenue growth, margins, guidance), commercial proof (named customers, contracts, capacity), survival and dilution (runway, share count, warrants), market position, early market recognition (relative strength, accumulation), and failure fingerprints. Then build the look-alike group: companies with the same visible profile on the same dates that did NOT run, and count how many went to zero or delisted. Output is a precursor scorecard (how many winners found, how many false positives, capital lost following them), not a buy rule. A rule follows only if the profile is rare among non-winners and survives the normal gates with months-long holds and the loss-line exit. No re-fitting the profile against the same winners.
strategies.status: studied (Squad 4, 2026-10-23): a precursor scorecard, not a buy rule
strategies.note: From the owner's aim of 22 Oct and three outside reviews the same day (look-alikes, point-in-time data, failure fingerprints, sustained vs peak). 'No actionable profile' is a valid and useful result.
strategies.squad4Spec: B-100X1 as run by Squad 4 (squad4-lab.mjs, specified 24 Oct 2026 before the run): WINNER = a stock whose close HELD 5x (or 10x) a starting close for 20 sessions (lowest close of 20 sessions, 15+ present), starting from any session at which it closed >= 2 USD with 20-session average volume >= 200k shares, within the 5-year data (adjusted prices; delisted stocks included; a path with a near-whole 3x-50x one-day jump = unadjusted split is ignored). SNAPSHOTS at the month starts 12, 6 and 3 months before the start of the move (the low it rose from) and at the start: revenue growth and acceleration, gross margin and trend, R&D intensity, market cap, 12-month return percentile, distance from the 52-week high, industry (SIC), officer/director ownership, share count change. LOOK-ALIKES: every eligible stock at the same month start with the same visible profile bucket (revenue growth band, 12-month return tercile, market-cap band, gross-margin trend), followed to the end of the data: how many reached 5x, how many died. PRECISION: monthly panel Oct 2022 - Sep 2024, each eligible stock followed 2 years (504 sessions): for each pre-listed profile the share that reached sustained 5x / 10x, the share that died or fell 80%+, lift over all stocks. A study, not a buy rule; no profile is re-fitted on these winners.

strategies.name: Run-up into a scheduled biotech/medtech catalyst (PDUFA date, advisory committee, topline readout), sold before the event
strategies.explain: The owner's OCGN case (23 Oct 2026). SOURCE: SEC EDGAR full-text search (efts.sec.gov, official), form 8-K incl. its exhibits (EX-99 press releases), filings from 2021-06-01, companies whose EDGAR SIC is 2833-2836, 3841-3845, 3851, 8731 or 8071; searched phrases "PDUFA", "target action date", "advisory committee", "topline", "top-line". DATE EXTRACTION, inside the sentence with the keyword (nearest date to the keyword): "Month D, YYYY" = that day; "Month YYYY" = the 1st of that month; "first/second/third/fourth quarter (of) YYYY", "Q1-Q4 YYYY", "1Q-4Q YYYY" = the 1st day of that quarter; "first/second half (of) YYYY", "1H/2H/H1/H2 YYYY" = the 1st day of that half (the earliest day the event could happen, so the sale is always before it). Vague timing ("mid-2025", "year-end", "2025", "early 2025") is not used. A topline sentence must also say expect/anticipate/plan/on track/guidance/remain/scheduled/intend/will. The event date must be after the filing date. RULE (ONE window, fixed now): event session s = first trading session on or after the event date; BUY at the open of session s-30; SELL at the close of session s-2 (29 sessions held; never held through the binary event). The catalyst counts only if a filing dated on a session BEFORE the entry session stated it (point in time; EDGAR gives the filing date only). One trade per (company, event date); one open trade per stock (an overlapping later event is skipped). CIK -> ticker: EDGAR display name ticker plus Massive reference tickers (active and delisted) by CIK, the one with a price on the entry day. GATES (all fixed now): whole US market incl. dead stocks (5-year whole-market cache study-cache/grouped.json.gz; its rows hold stocks at 3 USD+ with 1M USD+ traded, so the 2 USD entry floor is in practice 3 USD; exits use the dead-stock x rows); at the signal close: price 2 USD+ and 20-day average dollar volume 2M USD+; EXCLUDED if the company filed a 424B5, S-1, S-1/A, S-3 or S-3/A (EDGAR quarterly full index, filing date) in the 20 sessions before the entry session (dilution); EXCLUDED if the stock closed 15%+ above its previous close on any of the 21 sessions up to the signal close (house lottery rule). Halal is NOT applied in the test (data/halal.json + ZAD at the live stage only). Costs 0.8% per round trip (stress 1.2%). JUDGED FOR PROVEN and TRADABLE SMALL (tier 2): sessions split into an older and a newer half; 20+ trades in each half needed for any verdict; in BOTH halves: average net after 0.8% AND after 1.2% above 0, edge vs the average stock (3 USD+, 1M USD+ a day, bought the same day for the same sessions) above 0 with date-clustered t >= 2.5 (one average per entry day), better than the same stock on its other days in the same half (vsOwn > 0), still above 0 without its 2 best trades. All of that = TRADABLE SMALL; plus t >= max(own bar 2.5, league bar from data/agent-league.json, 4.0) in both halves = PROVEN. Edge above 0 in both halves but a gate missed = NOT PROVEN; otherwise REJECTED. Reported: trades, distinct days, stocks, win rate, average and median net, worst trade, each half, vs average stock, vs same stock, vs S&P 500 (information), without 2 best, t. RUN ONCE AS WRITTEN: the first complete verdict is frozen in firstRun (first-run.mjs); later runs are monitoring only. One version; no tuning after the first run.
strategies.note: Pre-registered before any run (23 Oct 2026). Built in catalyst-lab.mjs. Information only, no separate verdicts: the same numbers split by kind (PDUFA / advisory committee / topline) and by date precision (day / month / quarter / half). AUDIT 23 Oct (main session, after an outside review): the worst losses (QTTB -91%, SAVA -87%, FGEN -86%, RNA -82%, AMLX -80%) are all TOPLINE events with only a month/quarter/half date. The rule set such an event to the first day of its period, but these companies released results BEFORE that day, inside the holding window (e.g. SAVA's Phase 3 failure on 25 Nov 2024 vs a sell date of 27 Nov). So the rule sometimes held through the binary event it meant to avoid: a design flaw for imprecise dates. It does not change the verdict: exact-day events alone were 254 trades, edge +0.42%, t 0.33, and PDUFA dates alone t 1.06, both far below 2.5. Also: the stated 2 USD floor is effectively 3 USD (the price cache starts at 3 USD).

strategies.name: News build-up: 3+ positive company 8-Ks in 60 sessions, none negative, above the 50-day average; hold 15 sessions
strategies.explain: The "series of earlier news building up" half of the owner's OCGN case (23 Oct 2026). SOURCE: SEC EDGAR full-text search, form 8-K (incl. exhibits), all companies, filings from 2021-03-01. POSITIVE 8-K = a filing containing any of (fixed now): "Fast Track designation", "Breakthrough Therapy designation", "Orphan Drug designation", "Rare Pediatric Disease designation", "Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy", "Breakthrough Device designation", "positive topline", "positive top-line", "met its primary endpoint", "met the primary endpoint", "achieved its primary endpoint", "achieved the primary endpoint", "first patient dosed", "completed enrollment", "completion of enrollment", "awarded a contract", "contract award", "strategic partnership", "strategic collaboration", "collaboration and license agreement", "license and collaboration agreement", "exclusive license agreement", "supply agreement", "purchase order". NEGATIVE 8-K = a filing containing any of: "complete response letter", "clinical hold", "did not meet the primary endpoint", "did not meet its primary endpoint", "failed to meet", "did not achieve", "substantial doubt", "going concern", "Termination of a Material Definitive Agreement", "Notice of Delisting", "Non-Reliance on Previously Issued", "refusal to file", "discontinue development", "reduction in force", "workforce reduction". A filing with both counts as negative only. Each filing counts once. TIME: EDGAR gives the filing date only (read with sec-time.mjs secNY, date-only values = New York dates); an 8-K is known at the close of the first session on or after its filing date. RULE: signal at the close of session t when 3+ distinct positive 8-Ks are known within sessions t-59..t, no negative 8-K is known in that window, and the close is above its 50-day average close; BUY the next open (t+1), SELL at the close of t+15. One open trade per stock. GATES (all fixed now): whole US market incl. dead stocks (5-year whole-market cache study-cache/grouped.json.gz; its rows hold stocks at 3 USD+ with 1M USD+ traded, so the 2 USD entry floor is in practice 3 USD; exits use the dead-stock x rows); at the signal close: price 2 USD+ and 20-day average dollar volume 2M USD+; EXCLUDED if the company filed a 424B5, S-1, S-1/A, S-3 or S-3/A (EDGAR quarterly full index, filing date) in the 20 sessions before the entry session (dilution); EXCLUDED if the stock closed 15%+ above its previous close on any of the 21 sessions up to the signal close (house lottery rule). Halal is NOT applied in the test (data/halal.json + ZAD at the live stage only). Costs 0.8% per round trip (stress 1.2%). JUDGED FOR PROVEN and TRADABLE SMALL (tier 2): sessions split into an older and a newer half; 20+ trades in each half needed for any verdict; in BOTH halves: average net after 0.8% AND after 1.2% above 0, edge vs the average stock (3 USD+, 1M USD+ a day, bought the same day for the same sessions) above 0 with date-clustered t >= 2.5 (one average per entry day), better than the same stock on its other days in the same half (vsOwn > 0), still above 0 without its 2 best trades. All of that = TRADABLE SMALL; plus t >= max(own bar 2.5, league bar from data/agent-league.json, 4.0) in both halves = PROVEN. Edge above 0 in both halves but a gate missed = NOT PROVEN; otherwise REJECTED. Reported: trades, distinct days, stocks, win rate, average and median net, worst trade, each half, vs average stock, vs same stock, vs S&P 500 (information), without 2 best, t. RUN ONCE AS WRITTEN: the first complete verdict is frozen in firstRun (first-run.mjs); later runs are monitoring only. One version; no tuning after the first run.

strategies.name: Hot layer of an active chain: buy the members of the 3 strongest chain layers (3-month return vs S&P 500) that are above their 50-day average; hold 1 month

strategies.name: Repetition: does one chain layer lead another by a month? Pairs learned on the FIRST half only, traded on the SECOND half only
strategies.explain: The owner's sources claim AI leadership moved down the stack by scarcity (2023 chip designers, 2024 power and networking, 2025-26 memory, optics and equipment); this tests whether such an order repeats and can be traded. strategies.explain: SIGNAL: each NEW V15 pick (F-score 8-9 AND close above its own 200-day average; quality.mjs monthly formation every 21 sessions, the same picks the V15 test bought: every stock scoring 8-9, or the 10 best scores if under 10); NEW = not in the previous formation's picks. ENTRY: the next session's open after the formation day. EXPIRY: the earliest listed expiry 60-90 calendar days after the entry session. EXIT: the earlier of the V15 stock rule exit (126 sessions, as tested) and the last session on or before expiry minus 21 calendar days. B = 63 sessions. COMMON TO ALL FOUR (fixed 23 Oct 2026, before any run; options-core.mjs + options-lab.mjs). LONG CALLS ONLY, 1 contract. DATA: option prices = Alpaca historical DAILY option bars (v1beta1/options/bars, trade prices; history from about Jan-Feb 2024); contracts = Alpaca /v2/options/contracts (active and expired); underlying = Alpaca daily stock bars, RAW (strike choice, intrinsic value) and SPLIT-ADJUSTED (stock yardstick); sessions = SPY bars. Alpha Vantage HISTORICAL_OPTIONS (bid/ask, volume, open interest) is NOT available: the repo key is the free tier (premium endpoint refused, 25 requests a day, 1 a second); Alpaca has no historical option quotes (endpoint answers 404); Massive option aggregates are not in the plan (403). CONTRACT: on the entry session, among the calls of the rule's expiry, the strike nearest the underlying's raw open that has a daily bar ON the entry session (the 8 nearest strikes are tried; tie = lower strike); none = "no price" (counted, not traded). PRICES: entry = that bar's open x (1 + h); exit = the contract's close on the exit session x (1 - h); no bar on the exit session = intrinsic value max(0, raw close - strike) x (1 - h) (a floor; a call is worth at least that). A split during the hold (raw/adjusted ratio changes) excludes the trade (counted). SPREAD h = half the ask-bid spread as a share of the mid, MEASURED on the run day from Alpaca option snapshots (latest quote, indicative feed): per underlying the median (ask-bid)/mid of the 6 calls nearest the money in the rule's expiry window, h = max(2%, that / 2); an underlying with no usable quote today = the 75th percentile h of the rule's measured underlyings (5% if none). STRESS = 1.5 x h. Known limit: today's spread applied to the past. FEE: ZAD 5 USD per contract each side: net = (100 x exit - 5) / (100 x entry + 5) - 1. YARDSTICK (same money at risk): the same stock bought at the same session's open and sold at the same exit session's close (split-adjusted), minus 0.8% a round trip. HALVES: distinct entry sessions split at the median. JUDGED (verdictOf in options-core.mjs): 20+ priced trades in each half; in BOTH halves average net > 0 at h AND at the 1.5h stress, and above the same-money stock yardstick; still > 0 without its 2 best trades (whole period); t >= 2.5 over NON-OVERLAPPING blocks of B sessions (block = floor(entry session / B); a block's value = the average of its per-entry-day averages of net; 3+ blocks needed) = TRADABLE SMALL (tier 2); plus block t >= max(2.5, league bar from data/agent-league.json, 4.0) = PROVEN; edge over the stock > 0 in both halves but a gate missed = NOT PROVEN; else REJECTED; under 20 in a half = TOO FEW CASES. NOT applied in the test (live stage only): halal (data/halal.json "ok" only), the 300 USD premium cap (the <= 300 USD subset is reported for information), at most 2 open. Hold 40 sessions; stop 20%. Gate implemented in catalyst-integrity.mjs (assessCatalystImpact; missing data never passes). Exact-day dates only (parseEventDatePrecision).

strategies.name: Darvas box: buy-stop over a confirmed box top at a 52-week high, stop under the box bottom, raised box by box
strategies.explain: Nicolas Darvas (How I Made $2,000,000 in the Stock Market (1960)). RULE: Darvas box. Box top H = the highest high of t-25..t-1, made 4+ sessions ago with 3 lower highs after it, and a 52-week high; box bottom B = the lowest low after the top, made 4+ sessions ago (3 higher lows after it). Buy-stop at H (fills during t, at the open if it gaps over). Stop just under the box bottom (0.995 B). Trail: each new box that forms above (top confirmed by 3 lower highs, bottom by 3 higher lows) lifts the stop under its bottom. Max 504 sessions. No market filter. RECORD: self-reported (his 1960 book: about 2M USD in 18 months; press coverage, no statements). SOURCE: https://www.wallstreetmojo.com/darvas-box-theory. (48 versions) Exit set on the batch-1 entries QBO / PB / VCP / EP (their own entries, entry filters and skips unchanged). Stop DL = the day low (buy-stop entries: the entry-day low, from day 2, booked as stopped at 1 ADR if the entry day fell more than 1 ADR; open entries: the signal-day low) or 2A = 2 x 14-day ATR under the fill. Trail L10 = intraday under the 10-day low, E21 = next open after a close under the 21-day EMA, S50 = next open after a close under the 50-day. P = sell half at fill + 3R; N = no partial. Max 252. THIS VERSION: stop 2A, trail S50, partial none. One of 48 versions; all count toward the luck bar.

strategies.name: Hold, no stop, sell only on a close 5% (or 10%) above the buy; max 252 or 504 sessions
strategies.explain: Owner 23 Oct 2026: many traders hold a losing stock instead of selling and later sell with a win or the gap closes. RULE: buy at the open; no stop; sell at the next open after the first close >= buy +5% (version GE5) or +10% (GE10); otherwise sell at the close of session 252 (or 504) after the buy. Four versions: GE5/252, GE5/504, GE10/252, GE10/504, on every entry set (a, b1, b2, c, e). REPORT: % recovered (target reached), median sessions to recover, % still under water at the max, % paid out on vanishing, % dead, worst losses, worst open loss on the way, return per year of capital tied up vs SPY and SPUS over the SAME days. YARDSTICK (own): stocks = the same buy with the system 35% disaster stop held to the same max (X1, the rule for own picks); fund dip sets = the same fund with the same rule bought every 5th session in the same half (is buying the dip better than buying any day); fund all-days sets = the 35% stop version. Information: plain buy-and-hold to the same max.

strategies.name: Dip in a leader while the market is afraid
strategies.explain: industry top-3 by market cap, 30%+ under its 52-week high, S&P 500 15%+ under its high, revenue still growing; hold 12 months, add on -15%. RULE: Signal at the close of t: SPY close <= 85% of its highest close of the last 252 sessions; the stock is an industry LEADER; its close <= 70% of its highest close of the last 252 sessions (90%+ of them present); TTM revenue (SEC, filed before t, period ended <= 200 days before) above the TTM a year earlier. Universe: US companies filing quarterly SEC share counts, one ticker per company, liquid (close >= 5 USD, 20-session traded value >= 5M USD); market cap = close x shares known (30 days late, unadjusted split jumps repaired); industry = SIC 4-digit (current code); LEADER = top 3 by market cap of an industry with 5+ members that day. PLAN: 1 unit at the next open, +0.5 unit at the next open after the first close <= first buy -15%, sell all at the next open after the position is worth <= 65% of the money in (35% disaster stop on the total), else at the close of session 252; one open position per stock. Cost 0.8% per unit (1.2% stress). Judged at the tier-2 standard (both halves before / from 2024-01-01, vs the average stock over the same days, vs the same stocks with the same plan on other days, without the 2 best, block t >= 2.5 on 63-session blocks) plus return per year of capital tied up above the S&P 500 over the same days in both halves. strategies.name: Insider cluster with a size floor and an officer (3+ insiders, 300k USD+, 30 days)
strategies.explain: SEC Form 4 open-market purchases (code P, acquired, price > 0) by officers, directors or "other" insiders (a reporting owner that is ONLY a 10% owner, usually a fund, is left out). A cluster fires on the filing date d when, in the 30 calendar days ending d, 3+ different such insiders bought, together 300,000 USD+, and at least one of them is an OFFICER. Buy the next open after d; hold 63 sessions; one open trade per stock; after a cluster fires, the same stock cannot fire again for 30 days. Paper(s): Alldredge & Blank (2019) Do Insiders Cluster Trades With Colleagues? Evidence From Daily Insider Trading, Journal of Financial Research 42(2); Cohen, Malloy & Pomorski (2012) Decoding Inside Information, Journal of Finance 67(3). Reported: clustered insider purchases are followed by abnormal returns of over 2% in the next month (Alldredge & Blank 2019).
strategies.status: tested: rejected; forward paper lane from 26 Oct 2026

strategies.name: Insiders buy while short sellers stay away (2+ insiders 100k USD+, short interest under 3% and not rising)
strategies.explain: SEC Form 4 open-market purchases (code P) by officers / directors / other insiders (10%-only owners left out): 2+ different insiders in the 30 calendar days ending the filing date d, together 100,000 USD+. AND the FINRA short interest known on d (published ~14 days after settlement) is under 3% of the share count known (30 days late) AND not higher than the report about a month earlier (2 reports back). Buy the next open after d; hold 63; one open trade per stock; 30-day cooldown per stock. Short interest is used as the AVOID filter the research queue asked for. Paper(s): Chung, Sul & Wang (2019) Insider trading and short selling: combining the signals of informed traders, Journal of Portfolio Management (summary: Alpha Architect); Boehmer, Jones & Zhang (2008) Which Shorts Are Informed? Journal of Finance 63(2). Reported: combining insider demand and short-selling signals earned 1.27% in the next month and 2.03% in the next year (1977-2014); heavily shorted stocks underperform.

strategies.name: Buyback authorization of 5%+ of the company (8-K text)
strategies.explain: SEC EDGAR full-text search of 8-Ks (incl. exhibits) for board buyback-authorization phrases (BUYBACK_PHRASES); the matching document is read and the authorized size taken from sentences that name a repurchase / buyback AND an authorization / approval: the largest dollar amount ($ N million / billion) and the largest "up to N shares"; size = max(dollars / (share count known x close before entry), shares / share count known). Size 5%+ (40%+ = a parsing error, left out). First such filing per company in 180 days. Buy the next open after the filing date; hold 63; one open trade per stock. strategies.name: Customer momentum from 10-K major-customer disclosures
strategies.explain: Monthly (first session of the month): suppliers with an ACTIVE major-customer link in data/chain-graph.json (type customer: the supplier's own 10-K / 10-Q text naming the customer next to a concentration word; active from the first session after the first filing showing it until 400 days after the latest such filing on or before the day). Customer return = average return of the linked customers over the last 21 sessions. Liquid suppliers ranked by customer return; buy the top 20% (at least 10 ranked suppliers that month, else the month is skipped) at the next open; hold 21. Paper(s): Cohen & Frazzini (2008) Economic Links and Predictable Returns, Journal of Finance 63(4). Reported: buying suppliers whose major customers rose most last month and selling those whose customers fell earned ~1.5% a month (1981-2004); the supplier reacts late to its customer's news.

strategies.name: Analyst consensus turns more bullish (buy share up 15+ points in 3 months)
strategies.explain: Monthly (first session of month m): Finnhub recommendation trends (monthly counts of strong buy / buy / hold / sell / strong sell). Using only the snapshots of months BEFORE m: now = the snapshot of month m-1, before = month m-4. Bullish share = (strong buy + buy) / all; 5+ analysts in both; bullish share up 0.15+; liquid. strategies.name: Growth leader at a new high
strategies.explain: revenue +30%+ and accelerating, gross margin rising, within 5% of the 52-week high; hold 12 months, 35% disaster stop, 50-day trail after +100%. RULE: Monthly: TTM revenue growth >= 30%; latest quarter YoY growth above the prior quarter YoY growth; TTM gross margin above the TTM a year earlier; close >= 95% of the 52-week high. Buy every match. PLAN G: 1 unit at the next open; sell at the next open after a close at which the position is worth <= 65% of the money in (35% disaster stop); once a close has put it at +100% or more, sell at the next open after a close under its 50-session average; else sell at the close of session 252. Universe at the close of t: US-listed common stocks with an SEC company number (historical ticker map from the SEC Form 3/4/5 data sets, else the SEC ticker list), one ticker per company (the most traded), close >= 5 USD and 20-session average traded value >= 5M USD; dead and delisted stocks included. Fundamentals: SEC XBRL company facts point in time (filed BEFORE t; latest period ended <= 200 days before t). TTM revenue growth = TTM vs the TTM a year earlier (same tag); accelerating = the latest quarter YoY growth above the prior quarter YoY growth; gross margin = gross profit (else revenue - cost of revenue) / revenue, TTM, vs the TTM a year earlier; near the 52-week high = close >= 95% of the highest close of the last 252 sessions. Formation = the first session of each month (monthly overlapping cohorts); buy at the next open; one open position per stock per rule. Cost 0.8% per unit (1.2% stress). Judged once (first complete run frozen) at the tier-2 standard: both halves (signal before / from 2024-01-01; the first signal is possible about 12 months into the data, Oct 2022, so the older half is Oct 2022 - Dec 2023): > 0 after 0.8% and 1.2%, better than the average liquid stock over the same unit-weighted days, better than the same stocks with the same plan on their other days, > 0 without the 2 best, 20+ trades and 3+ blocks, block t >= 2.5 on 63-session blocks; plus return per year of capital tied up above SPY over the same days in both halves. Returns uncapped on both sides (a path with a near-whole 3x-50x one-day jump = an unadjusted split is left out on both sides); the +300% cap on both sides is reported as a sensitivity. Reported: return per year vs SPUS / HLAL, payoff distribution, share of profit from the top 5% of picks, information plans FORGET (no stop), STOP_ONLY, TWO_YEARS (504 sessions, no stop).

strategies.explain: RULE: Weekly, on the first session of each week that falls on a Wednesday or later (his Wednesday). Universe: the 500 most traded liquid stocks (S&P 500 proxy). SELL (next open) a held stock that leaves the top 20%, closes under its 100-day average, has a 15%+ move, or leaves the universe. BUY (next open), only when SPY closes above its 200-day average: from the top of the ranking down, stocks not held that pass the filters, each sized 0.1% of the account / ATR(20) (ATR as a fraction of the close; capped at 10% of the account), while the summed sizes fit in 100%; the first one that does not fit stops the buying. strategies.name: Winner DNA study: what big winners showed the day before, versus matched look-alikes (5-year whole market, discovery on the older half)
strategies.explain: A STUDY, not a buy rule. Winners = liquid stocks that closed +30% within 20 sessions (W20) or +100% within 120 sessions (W120) of the next open; up to 5 look-alikes per winner on the same day (same price band, liquidity band, prior 20-day move band and SIC 2-digit sector) that did not win; 31 features known at the close; lift, AUC and whole-market winner / loser rate and forward return per decile, older half (2021-10 to 2023-12) only. Finding: the strongest winner traits are variance traits (wide range, high volatility, far under the high, gaps, a down day, short base, dilution, small size) and they flag losers just as often (negative forward returns). Result file: data/squad7-dna.json; candidate screen data/squad7-screen.json.

strategies.name: The 20 largest companies, equal weight, quarterly
strategies.explain: the 20 largest US companies by market value, equal weight, re-formed every quarter (cap-weighted twin reported). RULE: Quarterly: the 20 largest by market value; equal weight, reset to equal at every quarter. Cap-weighted twin (same members) reported as information. Universe at the close of formation session t: liquid US stocks (close >= 5 USD, 20-session average traded value >= 5M USD; dead and delisted included) that map to an SEC company with revenue facts (operating companies; ETFs, funds and SPACs out), one ticker per company; market value = close x SEC share count known 30+ days before t (split-repaired; else the balance-sheet / weighted-average count from its filing date). Data guards: US companies only (SEC business address in a US state, no 20-F / 40-F filings; current SEC address), a market value is used only if 20-session traded value >= 0.02% of it and it is < 20,000B; a cover-page share count more than 3x off the financial-statement count (weighted-average shares from the filing date) is replaced by the latter. Formation at the first session of the month (quarterly: Jan / Apr / Jul / Oct); trades at the next open; cash at 0%. NO point-in-time halal status exists in the repository (data/halal.json = the owner's recent marks, zad-list = one quarterly change list): the test runs on the whole liquid market; today's members carry the owner's ZAD mark. PORTFOLIO: one account, 0.4% cost per buy and per sale (stress 0.6%), turnover of every rebalance counted, daily marks, dead stock = 0; monthly returns, CAGR, max drawdown, halves (start - end 2023 / 2024 - last close) vs SPY (price, like the stocks), SPUS, HLAL and the equal-weight average liquid stock. RULE: As SQ5-TOP20; at every month start, SPY close below its 200-session average -> sell all at the next open, hold cash at 0%; back above -> buy the current top 20 at the next open; quarterly resets while invested. Universe at the close of formation session t: liquid US stocks (close >= 5 USD, 20-session average traded value >= 5M USD; dead and delisted included) that map to an SEC company with revenue facts (operating companies; ETFs, funds and SPACs out), one ticker per company; market value = close x SEC share count known 30+ days before t (split-repaired; else the balance-sheet / weighted-average count from its filing date). Data guards: US companies only (SEC business address in a US state, no 20-F / 40-F filings; current SEC address), a market value is used only if 20-session traded value >= 0.02% of it and it is < 20,000B; a cover-page share count more than 3x off the financial-statement count (weighted-average shares from the filing date) is replaced by the latter. Formation at the first session of the month (quarterly: Jan / Apr / Jul / Oct); trades at the next open; cash at 0%. NO point-in-time halal status exists in the repository (data/halal.json = the owner's recent marks, zad-list = one quarterly change list): the test runs on the whole liquid market; today's members carry the owner's ZAD mark. PORTFOLIO: one account, 0.4% cost per buy and per sale (stress 0.6%), turnover of every rebalance counted, daily marks, dead stock = 0; monthly returns, CAGR, max drawdown, halves (start - end 2023 / 2024 - last close) vs SPY (price, like the stocks), SPUS, HLAL and the equal-weight average liquid stock. PER-TRADE JUDGE: each holding period = one trade (a stock from one review of the rule to its next review: quarter / month / the whole 6-month entry for SQ5-NEWIN; a sale, cash switch, delisting or the last close ends it early; still held = marked at the last close), the full 0.8% cost on every period (1.2% stress; conservative: what a TRY SMALL buy of one member for one period pays), halves by period start before / from 2024-01-01, value-core + hold-core judgeHold: > 0 after both costs, better than the average liquid stock over the same days, better than the same stock held as long on its other days, > 0 without the 2 best, 20+ trades and 3+ blocks, block t >= 2.5 (63-session blocks), return per year of capital above SPY on the same days in both halves; every gross return (rule and yardsticks) capped at +300% (AUD-1 capBoth). Run once, first complete verdict frozen.

Universe at the close of formation session t: liquid US stocks (close >= 5 USD, 20-session average traded value >= 5M USD; dead and delisted included) that map to an SEC company with revenue facts (operating companies; ETFs, funds and SPACs out), one ticker per company; market value = close x SEC share count known 30+ days before t (split-repaired; else the balance-sheet / weighted-average count from its filing date). strategies.name: Runner pullback: a 10-day runner bought on its first 8-15% pullback within 5-15 sessions, above its base and 20-day average (hold 20)
strategies.explain: RUNNER at the close of t (squad 8 base, unchanged: liquid; 10-session gain +15% to +100%; the first session it crosses +15%; complete data). PULLBACK: H_u = the highest close from t to u; the signal is the FIRST session u in t+5..t+15 with 0.85 x H_u <= close_u <= 0.92 x H_u (8-15% off the post-run high), close_u above the pre-run base (close of t-10) and above its 20-session average, liquid at u. The setup is void if before u any close (t+1..u-1) fell under 0.85 x H or under the pre-run base. Buy the open of u+1; hold 20 sessions; one open trade per stock. Paper(s): Jegadeesh (1990) Evidence of Predictable Behavior of Security Returns, Journal of Finance 45(3) (one-month reversal); Jegadeesh & Titman (1993) Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers, Journal of Finance 48(1); O'Neil, How to Make Money in Stocks (4th ed., 2009): buy a leader on its first orderly pullback, not extended (practitioner). Reported: one-month winners reverse (Jegadeesh 1990) while 3-12 month winners continue (Jegadeesh & Titman); practitioners buy a leader on its first orderly pullback rather than extended.

strategies.name: Leader then followers: the industry's largest member makes a new 52-week high right after its results 8-K; buy the next 2-4 largest that have not moved (hold 63)
strategies.explain: Industry (SIC 3-digit) with 4+ members in U_t (the 1,000 largest by 63-session traded value). LEADER = its member with the highest 63-session traded value at t. Signal at the close of the FIRST t in r0+1..r0+3 (always after the filing, whatever its hour) where the leader is still the leader and closes above its PRE-RESULTS 52-week high (the highest close of the 252 sessions before r0, 240+ present). Buy them at the open of t+1; hold 63 sessions; one open trade per stock. Journal of Accounting Research 46(4) (early reporters' news moves later peers); Foster (1981) Intra-industry information transfers associated with earnings releases, Journal of Accounting and Economics 3(3). Reported: news of the industry leader diffuses slowly to its peers (Hou 2007: big-firm returns lead small-firm returns of the same industry); an early reporter's results move its peers (Foster; Thomas & Zhang).

strategies.name: Big company: earnings gap-up of 3%+ that closes in the upper half of the day
strategies.explain: On the earnings reaction session R: open >= 3% above the previous close, close in the upper half of R's high-low range ((close - low) / (high - low) >= 0.5) and close above the previous close; a top-300 company. Signal = R; buy the open of R+1; hold 63. BIG = among the 300 largest US companies by point-in-time market value at the latest month start on or before the signal session (Squad 5 universe and market value: liquid US stocks, close >= 5 USD and 20-session traded value >= 5M USD, dead and delisted included, one ticker per company, CIK from the historical SEC Form 3/4/5 ticker map, US domicile, SEC share counts 30+ days old or from their filing date, split-repaired); events matched by the filer's CIK, never today's ticker list. Top-100 cut of the same events reported as information. Entry at the next open after the signal session; exit at the close of session 63; one open trade per stock; a stock that stops trading under 3 USD = 0. Earnings dates (amended before any result: the Nasdaq calendar cache has almost no before/after-open flags): the company's own SEC 8-K Item 2.02 by CIK with its EDGAR acceptance time on the New York clock; clock calibrated before any result on the opening gaps of 8,945 releases (many EDGAR stamps carry the New York offset twice): read hour < 14:00 = before the open (reaction that day), 16:00-17:59 or 20:00-21:59 = after the close (next session), other hours skipped; 8-K/A out. SEC XBRL values known from their filing date; event session = first session after the filing date. 8-K text: EDGAR full-text search (8-K incl. exhibits), filer CIK; confirmed = close of the first session after the filing date above the close of the last session before it. Cost 0.8% (1.2% stress); every gross return (rule and yardsticks) capped at +300% (AUD-1). Judged at the tier-2 standard (halves before / from 2024-01-01; > 0 after both costs, better than the average liquid stock on the same sessions, better than the same stock held 63 sessions on its other days, > 0 without the 2 best, 20+ trades and 3+ blocks, block t >= 2.5) plus return per year of capital above SPY on the same days in both halves; calendar-year table vs SPY reported. Run once, first complete verdict frozen. Paper(s): Brandt, Kishore, Santa-Clara & Venkatachalam (2008) Earnings announcements are full of surprises, SSRN 909563; Chan, Jegadeesh & Lakonishok (1996) Momentum Strategies, Journal of Finance 51(5); Zhou & Zhu (2012) Jump on the Post-Earnings Announcement Drift, Financial Analysts Journal 68(3). Reported: the stock's own reaction to earnings (announcement return) predicts drift over the next quarter; strongest when the reaction is a jump that holds.

strategies.name: Greenblatt magic formula (EBIT/EV + return on capital, 1000 largest, 10 a quarter, each held a year)
strategies.explain: RULE: Quarterly review. Universe: the 1000 largest, financials and utilities out. Earnings yield = EBIT / EV (EV > 0); return on capital = EBIT / (net working capital + net fixed assets), net working capital = (current assets - cash) - (current liabilities - current debt) floored at 0, net fixed assets = net property, plant and equipment; EBIT > 0 and capital > 0 needed. Rank each (1 = best), add the ranks, lowest sum first (ties: higher earnings yield). Each review buys the 10 best-ranked not held in the three younger sleeves; each sleeve is held one year (sold at the next open after the review four quarters later unless re-picked). About 40 holdings. DEVIATIONS from the published method: EBIT = operating income (no add-backs); a quarterly sleeve of 10 instead of "5-7 every 2-3 months"; market-value universe instead of the site's 50M+ screen (the book's 1000-largest version). Common (squad16-core.mjs header): universe = the N largest US operating companies by point-in-time market value at each review close (Squad 5 / 11 / 14 market value: SEC share count known 30+ days earlier x the close, dead stocks included, the historical Form 3/4/5 ticker map, US domicile, one ticker per company); SEC XBRL facts filed before the review only (TTM periods ended within 200 days). Baskets: bought at the next open after the review that selects them, held while selected, sold at the next open after the first review that drops them; sleeve rules hold each pick one year. Judged per REVIEW PERIOD (each stock held from the open after review j to the open after review j+1 is one trade, as Squad 5 periodPieces), so holdings still open today do not bias the result; every period pays the full 0.8% cost (1.2% stress); the portfolio test pays only real trades. strategies.name: Gray & Carlisle Quantitative Value (cheapest 10% by EV/EBIT, then the better half by Piotroski F-score, quarterly)
strategies.explain: RULE: Quarterly review. Universe: the 1000 largest, financials, utilities and REITs (SIC 6798, inside financials) out. strategies.name: COMEBACK BOARD: a rejected / not-proven rule can come back to TRY SMALL on its own forward paper record only
strategies.explain: RULE (comeback-core.mjs header): every lab rule with a frozen first-run verdict keeps its forward paper lane; only paper trades whose signal day is after that rule's frozenAt count (resolved by the lab at the rule's own hold and exits, 0.8% cost, 1.2% stress). COMEBACK = 30+ resolved trades on 10+ distinct signal days, average after 1.2% > 0, beats the average stock on the same days, beats SPY per year of capital, > 0 without its 2 best, block t >= max(2.5, one-sided z for 0.05 / N) where N = rules on the board with 30+ forward trades (Bonferroni), and both date halves of the forward record pass the TRY SMALL half gates. Near-copies of live rules (TRY_DUPLICATE), paused rules, baskets, intraday and options rules never come back. Frozen verdicts are never re-run or edited.
